properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js@1.1.7 is a transitive dependency of the ethereumjs/ethers stack in the client-starter and web3 dependency trees; it ships SHA-1, SHA-2 and RIPEMD-160 implementations whether or not this app calls them. No first-party call site found — dependency inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Transitive secp256k1 ECDSA engines (@noble/secp256k1 1.6.3, secp256k1 ^4.0.1) pulled in by the hardhat-toolbox/ethers toolchain of the web3/ Hardhat project — the dependency inventory: the build ships secp256k1 signing. The curve is fixed by the EVM (observable here, replaceable only at protocol level). App-level signing is wired separately via hardhat.config.ts accounts and the client's wallet signer. @types/secp256k1 is declarations only, but the object also covers the two real implementations

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: bcrypt-pbkdf turns bcrypt (EksBlowfish) into a PBKDF used for OpenSSH-style passphrase key derivation, and depends on tweetnacl; it sits in the web3 hardhat dependency tree. No first-party call site — dependency inventory. Changeable here via lockfile.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: evp_bytestokey ^1.0.3 ships in the web3/ dependency tree (transitive via the browserify/cipher-base chain inside hardhat-toolbox). The deprecated single-round-MD5 KDF is available to any code in that tree even though no application call site was found — presence is what this entry records.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Available in the shipped web3 dependency tree via bcrypt-pbkdf; no first-party call site found in application code — presence recorded as dependency inventory. Ed25519 is a Shor-vulnerable signature primitive: a deadline problem (migrate to ML-DSA on a schedule), not a harvest-now problem.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic 6.5.4 is the secp256k1 ECDSA engine that ethers v5 (@ethersproject/signing-key) uses; it ships in the client-starter build. Declared-but-unused in this template: client-starter/src never imports ethers (only window.ethereum account discovery) — dependency-inventory presence, no direct call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDH is part of the elliptic 6.5.4 API surface and ships with the client-starter build; no ECDH call site exists in client-starter/src. Availability of the primitive in the shipped tree is what this entry records.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl 0.14.5 (transitive in the web3/ hardhat toolchain) provides X25519 key agreement plus XSalsa20-Poly1305 secretbox; no application call site found — recorded as shipped capability of the tree.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @ethersproject/keccak256 ^5.7.0 is the EVM hash dependency of ethers v5 in all three projects (client, client-starter, web3) — used transitively for transaction hashing, ABI encoding and address derivation. The on-chain keccak256 use in AvaxGods.sol is a separate app-level asset I report as a finding; these lockfile sites record the shipped library.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ethers v5 uses @ethersproject/pbkdf2 (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256, ~262k iterations by default in keystore JSON) to encrypt/decrypt wallets; the plain pbkdf2 package backs the Node path. All 33 sites are lockfile declarations; iteration counts and salt parameters are not visible at these sites, only the capability. Changeable here via lockfile.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js is the password KDF ethers uses for JSON keystore wallets; versions 3.0.1 (ethers tree) and 2.0.4 (eth-gas-reporter subtree in web3/) ship in all three dependency trees. No direct app call site — dependency-inventory presence.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 is the workhorse hash across the ethereumjs/scure packages in the web3 tree. Dependency-capability inventory; no first-party call site found.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/hashes is pulled into the web3 hardhat tree by the ethereumjs/scure stack. Library API surface ships in node_modules; no first-party call site found, which is a limitation of this inventory, not evidence of non-use.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak/SHA-3 is core to Ethereum address and transaction hashing; @noble/hashes enters the web3 tree via ethereumjs packages. Dependency-capability inventory; no first-party call site found.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl's secretbox AE capability, shipping in the web3/ tree via the same declared package as the X25519 entry (ALG-defedad1). Recorded as available-in-shipped-library; no call site found in application code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl is the audited NaCl port providing Ed25519, X25519, XSalsa20-Poly1305 and SHA-512; it enters the web3 tree via bcrypt-pbkdf. Presence is the inventory question; no first-party call site found, which is a limitation of the inventory, not proof of non-use (reachable at runtime via any transitive caller).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/hashes is the modern hashing library used by the ethereumjs/scure packages in the hardhat tree (SHA-2, SHA-3/Keccak, BLAKE, RIPEMD). No first-party call site found — dependency inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Library/provider facet of the scrypt dependency in client-starter's lockfile — the same package entries the scrypt algorithm object (ALG-c1f8b585) records for client-starter/package-lock.json. Kept as the provider record so a reader can reference the library entry and the algorithm entry together.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Legacy stream-style SHA-1/SHA-2 implementation pulled by the ethereum tooling in the web3 tree. No first-party call site found — dependency inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto library shipping in the client-starter dependency tree; provides the ECDSA/ECDH recorded as ALG-710f61f0/ALG-c9ffc8a8. elliptic 6.5.x also has known signature-malleability advisories — worth a version bump when the starter is updated, but presence is what this entry records. No direct import in client-starter/src.

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Pure-JS PBKDF2 package in the web3 dependency tree (Node/browser keystore path), complementing @ethersproject/pbkdf2. No first-party call site found — dependency inventory.
